text:
Recent work supports testing multi-negative objectives before aggressive hard mining. “On the Effectiveness of Sampled Softmax Loss” (2024) finds temperature-sensitive behavior: excessively hard negatives can dominate gradients; its shared negative pools offer an efficient implementation. “Scalable Cross-Entropy” (RecSys 2024) approximates full softmax using informative catalog subsets. These motivate replacing single-negative training with sampled-softmax cross-entropy over multiple negatives while retaining NextItNet’s causal convolutional backbone. Neither establishes an Electronics-specific improvement. Sources: [sampled softmax paper](https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf), [SCE paper](https://dspace.mit.edu/entities/publication/5392aca9-0bae-4176-9b3a-a8165957ba26).

Hardness requires safeguards. A 2024 sequential-recommendation study comparing random, popularity, in-batch and adaptive sampling finds dataset-dependent accuracy and popularity-bias tradeoffs. UFNRec explicitly studies false negatives in sequential recommendation; 2026 EMM describes mixing hard/random negatives with ID exclusion and similarity-window filtering. Practical hypothesis for this task: compare uniform multi-negative softmax against a modest hard/random mixture mined using the same NextItNet model, exclude padding, targets and observed training positives, and tune temperature or hard-negative weight. Similarity filtering is a heuristic, not proof that an item is a false negative. Keep one trained checkpoint per category and select exclusively by fixed four-category macro validation HR@10; larger sampled margins alone provide no evidence of improvement. Sources: [sampling comparison](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276), [UFNRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116), [EMM](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0893608026004090).
